history.summary: A historical Shakti shrine about 2 km from Rudrapur on the Haldwani highway, dedicated to Goddess Atariya. Founded in the late 16th century by King Rudra Chand of the Chand dynasty, founder of Rudrapur. Legend says his royal chariot bogged down in Terai marshland here, and after fervent prayer to the Divine Mother he was guided to safety and consecrated this temple on a raised earthen mound ('Atta'), giving the shrine its name Atariya. CSV town corrected from 'Udham Singh Nagar' to Rudrapur. The grand 10-day Atariya Mela is held here every year during Chaitra Navratri (March-April).

name: Atariya Temple
town_description: Rudrapur is the district headquarters of Udham Singh Nagar, founded in the late 16th century by Chand king Rudra Chand and named after him. Situated in the Terai plains, it is the gateway to the Kumaon hills and a fast-growing industrial and trading city, while retaining historic religious sites such as the Atariya Temple.

travel.railway: Rudrapur City Railway Station, about 2.5 km
travel.road: About 2 km from Rudrapur bus station on the Rudrapur-Haldwani highway; well connected by road to Delhi, Dehradun and Nainital

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the Atariya Mela during Chaitra Navratri (March-April) is the liveliest time
